ma_stone_tower_boulder.blurb: A house-sized granite block in the Lynn Woods forest north of Boston, tucked just below the old stone observation tower that marks the middle of its bouldering zone. Problems wrap around every side, and the 24 lines here run from easy warm-ups through a solid middle band of V3 to V7, then climb into hard double-digit territory, so it suits strong boulderers more than newcomers. Most of the lines are described as high quality, enough to fill a half day or more on a single rock. The surrounding woods hold hundreds of other boulders, so it works as one stop on a longer circuit.
ma_stone_tower_boulder.approach: Walk in from the main lot on Great Woods Road, follow the trail uphill to the stone tower, pass it, then drop down a steep trail for a couple of minutes; the boulder sits off to the side.

ma_waitts_mountain_cliff_2.blurb: A small city-park cliff in Malden, close to Boston and handy by public transit, with views over the skyline. About two dozen climbs share the wall: roughly half are boulder problems, mostly in the easy V0 to V3 range, and the rest are short top-rope, trad and sport lines from low fifth-class up to the 5.11 range. Its modest difficulty and convenience make it a common choice for beginner outings and quick after-work sessions, rather than a destination for a full day.

ma_shoreline_goliath.blurb: The largest single boulder at Rocky Pond, a bouldering area in Boylston a short drive from Worcester. It is a big glacial erratic of gritty granite, roughly 30 by 60 feet and tall, sitting right beside the water. It carries more problems than any other block there: 23 lines that start with a single V0 and grow steadily through V2 to V5, with a few much harder problems at the top end. That spread makes it a good stop for mid-grade boulderers, while a handful of very hard lines give strong climbers something to try.
ma_shoreline_goliath.approach: From the trailhead, take the single track south, then follow the wide cleared path through the woods for about six minutes. Where it swings right and climbs, stay left on narrower trail, passing two named boulders, and the big block stands near the pond.

ma_c_wall_aka_c_face.blurb: A popular wall in the old granite quarries at Quincy, southeast of Boston, also nicknamed the Reflector Oven for the heat it collects in summer. It stands somewhere around 35 to 45 feet and is almost entirely top-rope, with 20 of its 22 climbs set up that way and just two trad lines. Grades sit mostly in the 5.7 to 5.9 range, with a few easier ones and some serious 5.12 lines for the keen. The compact granite can feel slick on hot days. Easy to reach and close to the city, it suits learners and anyone practising top-rope setups.

ma_berlin_boulder.blurb: A single large boulder beside the road in Garfield Woods, a conservation parcel in Berlin in eastern Massachusetts. It sits only a short stroll from a gravel pull-off, which makes it an easy quick session. The 22 problems range from a handful of V0 and V1 warm-ups through a middle group around V4 and V5 to a few hard V7 and V8 lines. Features include a roof and a cave-like section, and the problems are numbered around the block starting at its southeast corner. It stays well shaded, even in the cooler months, so it is more useful on warm days than cold ones.

ma_tatnuck_boulder.blurb: A small boulder in Worcester's Cascades park, reached by a short trail walk past a waterfall to a rock outcropping on the hilltop. It is a low-key spot for easy problems: about 21 lines, most between V0 and V4, with roughly eight at V2 and a smattering of beginner-level climbs. Some lines are slabby. It is a good quick stop in town for newer boulderers or a warm-up, while stronger climbers will want to head to the larger boulderfield at Rocky Pond, about a quarter hour away.

ma_granola_boulders.blurb: A small cluster of granite boulders on the east side of Dykes Pond in Gloucester, on Cape Ann. Two main blocks stand about fifty feet apart, with other boulders nearby that hold potential for more. The 21 problems cover V0 through V6, with the bulk in the V3 to V5 range, plus a few easy ones, and a few of its lines are well regarded. Some of the rocks in this part of the woods grow over, so a brush helps. It makes a good add-on to a circuit of the larger Dykes Pond boulderfield.
